statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the minimum value of q - p over all integer pairs (p, q) with 0 <= p <= q <= len(t) for which the concatenation of t[0..p) and t[q..len(t)) is a subsequence of s. Here t[0..p) is the byte sequence t[0],...,t[p-1] (empty if p=0), t[q..len(t)) is t[q],...,t[len(t)-1] (empty if q=len(t)), and a byte sequence u is a subsequence of s if there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < j_1 < ... < j_{len(u)-1} < len(s) with s[j_k] = u[k] for every k (the empty sequence is a subsequence of s). The set being minimized over is nonempty because p=0, q=len(t) gives the empty concatenation.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(t).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if t is a subsequence of s, where a byte sequence u is a subsequence of s if there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{len(u)-1} < len(s) with s[j_k] = u[k] for every k; in particular t is a subsequence of s if there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{len(t)-1} < len(s) with s[j_k] = t[k] for every k.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r > 0, there exist integers p and q with 0 <= p < q <= len(t) such that q - p = r and the concatenation of t[0..p) and t[q..len(t)) is a subsequence of s (where subsequence means there are strictly increasing indices in s matching the concatenated bytes in order).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every pair of integers (p, q) with 0 <= p <= q <= len(t) such that the concatenation of t[0..p) and t[q..len(t)) is a subsequence of s (with the standard order-preserving meaning), we have r <= q - p.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= len(t) - len(s).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122), and len(t) > len(s).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(s) and s[i] = t[0], and r = 1 otherwise.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122), and len(t) = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(t).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s) and every j with 0 <= j < len(t), s[i] != t[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(t) if and only if for every pair of integers (p, q) with 0 <= p <= q <= len(t) and q - p < len(t), the concatenation of t[0..p) and t[q..len(t)) is not a subsequence of s (with the standard order-preserving meaning).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if (a) t is not a subsequence of s, and (b) there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(t) such that the concatenation of t[0..i) and t[i+1..len(t)) (that is, t with the single character at index i deleted) is a subsequence of s.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 100000, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).

statement: Let c = s[0]. Whenever the function returns a result r: (1) if len(t) = 1 and t[0] = c, then r = 0; (2) if len(t) = 1 and t[0] != c, then r = 1; (3) if len(t) >= 2 and (t[0] = c or t[len(t)-1] = c), then r = len(t) - 1; (4) if len(t) >= 2 and t[0] != c and t[len(t)-1] != c, then r = len(t).
preconditions: len(s) = 1, len(t) >= 1, len(t) <= 100000, and every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= byte <= 122).
